content: I'll read the test image to analyze the visual symptoms.

Analyzing the image:

**Affected plant part:** Banana plant — leaves and lower pseudostem area visible.

**Key visual observations:**
- Large, relatively intact green banana leaf in the foreground
- The lower/outer portions of the plant show yellowing and collapsed, drooping leaf material
- Browning and wilting visible at the base/lower leaf area
- Leaves appear to be collapsing downward rather than showing discrete spots or lesions

**Reasoning through the classes:**

- **Anthracnose** — typically shows dark, sunken lesions on fruit; not matching
- **Bunchy_Top** — would show upright, bunched narrow leaves with dark green streaks; not evident here
- **Cigar_End_Rot** — affects fruit tips only; no fruit visible with those symptoms
- **Cordana_Leaf_Spot** — oval/tan spots with dark borders on leaf lamina; not the pattern here
- **Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka** — characterized by distinct yellow streaks or dark lesions with halos on leaf blade; not clearly matching
- **Panama_Disease** (Fusarium wilt) — causes yellowing of older/outer leaves progressing inward, leaves collapse and hang down, overall wilting and drooping of the plant. The yellowing and collapsed outer leaf material around the base strongly matches this pattern.

The collapsed, yellowing outer leaves draping downward around the base of an otherwise still-green banana plant is a hallmark presentation of Panama Disease (Fusarium oxysporum f.sp. cubense).
